title: Wire a host graph executor and submit an external job once
narrative: Fangore builds a host that dispatches a remote coding job from a durable plan. They need a short, readable way to register that job step, choose durable storage, and submit exactly once — including after a crash where the remote system may already have accepted the job. Complements `fangore_graph_executor` (authorized plan walk) and `fangore_transactional_durable_resume` (crash-window reconciliation). Host wiring lives in the dependency-injection guide[^host-kit-di].
implementation: `mechaharness.host_kit.host_graph_executor` subclasses `MechaHarnessConfig` and injects a `GraphExecutor` with host runners, default graph grants, optional `SqliteCheckpointStore` via `checkpoint_path` / `checkpoint_store`, and an injectable `CrashProbe`. `SubmitOnceEffectfulRunner` implements `EffectfulGraphNodeRunner` for submit-once / complete-on-accept / never-silent-redispatch of `UNCERTAIN` without a handle. `effectful_external_handle` reads the recorded handle from a `GraphResult` without scraping node maps. Module doctests document the blessed host path.
validation: Harness `harness_runs` op `host_kit_submit_once` → `_run_host_kit_submit_once`. Soft expects: durable dispatch status ok with one submit and a handle; resume of uncertain-with-handle completes with zero further submits. Unit matrix: `tests/fixtures/host_kit/*.json` via `tests/test_host_kit.py` and `tests/support/host_kit_cases.py` (ephemeral dispatch, uncertain-without-handle needs attention, accepted resume). Pytest `--doctest-modules` covers pydoc examples on `src/mechaharness/host_kit.py`.
